You are an accreditation coordinator preparing a comprehensive curriculum review for an upcoming university accreditation visit. Your job is to audit the institution's courses against accreditation requirements, find supporting scholarly literature, and document everything in a structured compliance matrix and an accreditation report.

Start by fetching the accreditation requirements from the accreditation portal at http://localhost:30238/api/accreditation_requirements.json. This document specifies minimum thresholds for course counts, faculty ratios, assessment types, and scholarly integration that the institution must meet.

Next, connect to the learning management system and retrieve a list of all courses offered by the institution. For each course, gather the course name, the number of enrolled students, the number of assignments, the number of quizzes the course has (use 0 if it has none), and the number of discussion topics. Also determine how many faculty members (teachers and teaching assistants combined) are associated with each course. Use the course's enrollment count (total students) directly for the number of enrolled students, and derive the faculty count from each course's enrollment records, where faculty are enrollments of type TeacherEnrollment or TaEnrollment.

Using this data, evaluate each course against the accreditation requirements. A course is considered compliant if the student to faculty ratio does not exceed the maximum specified in the requirements and the course has at least one form of assessment (quiz or assignment). Note which courses are compliant and which are not.

Then search the scholarly literature for research supporting the pedagogical approaches used in the curriculum. Search for papers on the following topics: active learning in higher education, assessment best practices in education, online learning effectiveness, curriculum design frameworks, and student engagement strategies. For each topic, find at least one relevant paper and note its title, authors, and relevance to the curriculum.

Create an Excel file called Curriculum_Review.xlsx in your workspace with three sheets. The first sheet should be called "Course Compliance" with columns for Course_Name, Assignment_Count, Quiz_Count, Discussion_Count, Student_Count, Faculty_Count, Student_Faculty_Ratio, and Compliant (Yes or No based on whether the course meets the accreditation criteria). Include all courses.

The second sheet should be called "Literature Support" with columns for Search_Topic, Paper_Title, Authors, and Relevance_Note. Include at least five rows covering the five pedagogical topics listed above.

The third sheet should be called "Summary" with columns for Metric and Value. Include rows for total courses, compliant courses, non-compliant courses, compliance rate (as a percentage), total faculty across all courses, average student to faculty ratio, and the number of supporting papers found.

Finally, create a page in the team's knowledge base (Notion) titled "Accreditation Review Report" (the page title must contain this exact phrase) that summarizes the curriculum audit findings. The page should mention the overall compliance rate, highlight any courses that fail to meet requirements, reference the scholarly literature that supports the institution's pedagogical approach, and note any recommendations for improvement before the accreditation visit.

When you have completed all tasks, call claim_done.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one parallel source wave and one parallel writer wave. Canvas and scholarly search are read-only. The main agent fetches the accreditation JSON and freezes the course manifest; writers consume only the merged canonical packet.

Before Wave 1, the main agent fetches http://localhost:30238/api/accreditation_requirements.json once and freezes the literal student-faculty-ratio maximum and assessment-presence rule. It then calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once, validates unique IDs/codes/full names, and freezes the complete 22-course manifest. Partition that manifest into two disjoint shards covering every course_id exactly once: shard A = course_id 1-11 (AAA-2013J through DDD-2013B) and shard B = course_id 12-22 (DDD-2014B through GGG-2014B). Pass each owner its literal ID list, codes, and full names.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 3 explore sub-agents in parallel:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Course-metrics owner for shard A (course_id 1-11). For each assigned course, collect the exact full name, enrolled-student count from the course enrollment total, assignment count, quiz count (0 if none), discussion-topic count, and faculty count (TeacherEnrollment plus TaEnrollment only), then mark it compliant when the student-faculty ratio stays within the frozen accreditation maximum and the course has at least one quiz or assignment. Faculty counts must come from actual enrollment records, never inferred from grade rows or current-user metadata; a course lacking source-visible student plus TeacherEnrollment/TaEnrollment coverage gets CONTRACT_BLOCKER_MISSING_ROLE_COMPLETE_ENROLLMENTS and no Faculty_Count, Student_Faculty_Ratio, or Compliant value. Return assigned versus observed course IDs plus the compact per-course rows. Make no writes.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Course-metrics owner for shard B (course_id 12-22) — same literal recipe, only that shard's course identities substituted.
   3. explore 2 (academic-literature-researcher 0): Literature owner for the five fixed pedagogy topics: active learning in higher education; assessment best practices in education; online learning effectiveness; curriculum design frameworks; and student engagement strategies. Find one genuinely relevant paper per topic and return title, authors, and a curriculum-relevance note for each. Read-only; do not write the workbook or Notion page.

After Wave 1, the main agent requires both shards together to cover every frozen course_id exactly once, rejects duplicate/missing IDs, and freezes one canonical packet: all 22 Course Compliance rows, at least five Literature Support rows, and the Summary metrics (total courses, compliant courses, non-compliant courses, compliance rate as a percentage, total faculty across all courses, average student-faculty ratio, supporting-paper count).

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming the canonical packet with no recomputation from Canvas or scholarly search:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Curriculum_Review.xlsx. Create exactly Course Compliance, Literature Support, and Summary with the task's exact headers, all 22 course rows, at least five literature rows, and the frozen summary metrics as literal values. Read every populated range back.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole Notion owner of a page whose title contains the exact phrase Accreditation Review Report. Search exact title first, create at most once on zero matches, block on duplicates, and write a summary of the overall compliance rate, non-compliant courses, scholarly literature supporting the pedagogical approach, and recommendations before the visit. Read the retained page and its child-block text back.

After Wave 2, the main agent reconciles workbook ranges and the Notion read-back against the same packet, then calls claim_done. Do not dispatch an aggregation or verification agent.

Your assigned Canvas course IDs: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6

| course_id | course_name | total_students |
| 1 | Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2013) | 383 |
| 2 | Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014) | 365 |
| 3 | Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2013) | 2237 |
| 4 | Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014) | 2292 |
| 5 | Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2013) | 1767 |
| 6 | Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014) | 1613 |

For EACH assigned course ID, make these read-only Canvas calls and count the items returned:
1. canvas_list_assignments(course_id=N) → number of assignment objects returned = Assignment_Count
2. canvas_list_quizzes(course_id=N) → number of quiz objects returned = Quiz_Count (use 0 if empty)
3. canvas_list_discussion_topics(course_id=N) → number of topic objects returned = Discussion_Count
4. canvas_get_course_grades(course_id=N, per_page=100, type=["TeacherEnrollment","TaEnrollment"]) → Faculty_Count. Read the "pagination" object: use pagination.total_count as the count, and if pagination.has_more is true, keep paging (page=2,3,...) until has_more is false and sum. Do NOT filter by enrollment_state — count every TeacherEnrollment and TaEnrollment row.

Note: count ALL items returned by each list endpoint, regardless of their "published" flag.

DELIVERABLE: Return a compact table (markdown or JSON) with exactly one row per course and these fields: course_id, course_name, assignment_count, quiz_count, discussion_count, faculty_count, total_students. Also list the faculty user_ids and enrollment types per course (a short list, useful for my audit). Do NOT paste full JSON dumps of assignments/quizzes/discussions. Flag any endpoint that errors or returns an empty list.

I am preparing a university accreditation curriculum review and need scholarly literature that supports the pedagogical approaches used in the curriculum. Use the scholarly/arXiv search tools available to you (read-only; do not change anything).

Search for papers on these FIVE topics (run one search per topic):
1. active learning in higher education
2. assessment best practices in education
3. online learning effectiveness
4. curriculum design frameworks
5. student engagement strategies

For EACH topic, find AT LEAST ONE relevant paper (aim for 1-2 solid matches per topic; prefer papers whose abstract genuinely matches the topic). For each paper record:
- Search_Topic (the topic label from the list above, exactly as written)
- Paper_Title (full title)
- Authors (all listed authors, in order; if there are more than 6, list the first 3 followed by "et al.")
- Relevance_Note (1-3 sentences explaining how the paper supports a curriculum/teaching approach for that topic — e.g., what it found or recommends)
- Publication year and venue/source if available

DELIVERABLE: Return a compact table or list with one entry per paper found, with the five fields above. Aim for at least 5 papers total (at least one per topic). Do not paste entire abstracts — just the title, authors, and your concise relevance note. If a search returns no results for a topic, say so explicitly and try a rephrased search.
Scholarly literature on 5 topics

Create a Notion page in the team knowledge base. This is an external write task — you have the Notion MCP write tools.

GOAL: Create a page titled exactly **"Accreditation Review Report"** (this exact phrase must be the page title) as a **child of the existing Notion page with ID `8e968e79-b7f2-4c97-9b6c-a855b092c345`** (that page is named "Accreditation Documents"). Then populate it with the report content below.

IMPORTANT TECHNICAL NOTES:
- The `parent` and `properties` parameters of `API-post-page` must be passed as **JSON objects, not strings**. If your first call fails schema validation, try: (a) creating the page with only `parent` + `properties` and no `children`, then adding the body with `API-patch-block-children` on the new page ID; (b) try passing parameters as JSON-encoded strings. Work through the formats until one succeeds — do not give up after one failure.
- Do NOT create the page anywhere else (not as a workspace-level page, not under any other parent) unless parenting under `8e968e79-b7f2-4c97-9b6c-a855b092c345` proves impossible; if you truly cannot, create it at workspace level and say so in your report.
- You may need multiple `API-patch-block-children` calls (Notion caps blocks per call ~100). Append sequentially so content order is preserved.
- Do not modify or archive any other existing pages.

=== REPORT CONTENT TO PUT ON THE PAGE (render as headings, paragraphs, bullets, numbered lists, and one table) ===

Opening paragraph:
"Curriculum audit prepared for the Higher Education Quality Council — Accreditation Standards Version 2025.1. All 22 courses offered by the institution were reviewed against the published accreditation requirements covering course counts, faculty ratios, assessment coverage, and scholarly integration."

HEADING: 1. Executive Summary
Paragraph: "This report documents a comprehensive curriculum audit of the institution's learning management system ahead of the upcoming accreditation visit. For every course we captured enrolment counts, assignment and quiz counts, discussion topic counts, and faculty staffing (teachers and teaching assistants combined), then evaluated each course against the accreditation requirements."
Paragraph: "The institution satisfies the institutional-level requirements: 22 courses are offered against a minimum of 15, every course has at least one faculty member, every course has at least one form of assessment, and five scholarly references were identified against a minimum of five. The single material weakness is staffing intensity — 4 of the 22 courses exceed the maximum permitted student-to-faculty ratio of 600:1 and are therefore non-compliant."

HEADING: 2. Overall Compliance Rate
Paragraph: "The overall course compliance rate is 81.82% — 18 of 22 courses are compliant and 4 are non-compliant."
Bullets:
- Total courses audited: 22
- Compliant courses: 18
- Non-compliant courses: 4
- Compliance rate: 81.82%
- Total faculty across all courses (teacher and TA enrolments): 70
- Average student-to-faculty ratio: 488.65:1 (permitted maximum: 600:1)
- Supporting scholarly papers identified: 5

HEADING: 3. Courses Failing to Meet Requirements
Paragraph: "Four courses exceed the maximum permitted student-to-faculty ratio of 600:1 and fail the accreditation criteria. Every course in the institution has at least one form of assessment, so no course fails on assessment coverage — all non-compliance is attributable to staffing ratios."
TABLE with columns: Course | Students | Faculty | Ratio | Status
Rows (in this order):
1. Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) | 2,283 | 2 | 1,141.50:1 | Non-compliant
2. Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014) | 2,498 | 3 | 832.67:1 | Non-compliant
3. Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014) | 1,613 | 2 | 806.50:1 | Non-compliant
4. Foundations of Finance (Spring 2014) | 1,500 | 2 | 750.00:1 | Non-compliant
(If creating a Notion table block proves difficult, fall back to a bulleted list with one bullet per course using the same pipe-separated text.)
Paragraph: "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) is the most serious outlier, running at nearly twice the permitted ratio with 2,283 students supported by only 2 faculty. A further governance concern: Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014) is staffed entirely by two teaching assistants with no teacher of record."

HEADING: 4. Institutional Requirements Assessment
Bullets:
- Minimum courses (15 required) — MET: 22 courses offered.
- Minimum faculty per course (1 required) — MET: every course has at least 2 faculty (teachers and teaching assistants combined).
- Assessment types (quiz, assignment, discussion) — PARTIALLY MET: all 22 courses have assignments and all 22 have discussion topics, but only 14 of 22 courses have quizzes; 8 courses currently have none.
- Student-to-faculty ratio maximum (600:1) — PARTIALLY MET: 4 of 22 courses exceed the ceiling.
- Research integration / minimum scholarly references (5 required) — MET: 5 supporting papers identified, one for each required pedagogical topic.

HEADING: 5. Scholarly Literature Supporting the Pedagogical Approach
Paragraph: "The curriculum's pedagogical design is well grounded in peer-reviewed literature. Five references were identified, covering each of the required pedagogical topics."
SUBHEADING: Active learning in higher education
Paragraph: "Freeman S, Eddy SL, McDonough M, et al. (2014), \"Active Learning Increases Student Performance in Science, Engineering, and Mathematics\", Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. A meta-analysis of 225 studies showing active learning raises exam performance by roughly half a standard deviation, while pure lecturing raises failure rates by 55% relative to active learning. This directly supports the institution's use of interactive, discussion-based pedagogy across all 22 courses and every discipline."
SUBHEADING: Assessment best practices in education
Paragraph: "Angelo TA & Cross KP (1993), \"Classroom Assessment Techniques: A Handbook for College Teachers\", Jossey-Bass. The definitive guide to formative and summative assessment in higher education, presenting 50 classroom assessment techniques for verifying what and how well students are learning. This supports the curriculum's layered assessment model of continuous computer-marked quizzes plus tutor-marked assignments."
SUBHEADING: Online learning effectiveness
Paragraph: "Means B, Toyama Y, Murphy R, Bakia M, Jones K (2009), \"Evaluation of Evidence-Based Practices in Online Learning: A Meta-Analysis and Review of Online Learning Studies\", US Department of Education. A systematic meta-analysis finding that students in online conditions performed modestly better than those in face-to-face instruction, with blended approaches showing the largest advantages. This provides the evidence base for the institution's online and blended delivery model."
SUBHEADING: Curriculum design frameworks
Paragraph: "Wiggins G & McTighe J (2005), \"Understanding by Design: A Framework for Curriculum Development\", ASCD. Introduces backward design — begin with desired learning outcomes, then determine acceptable evidence, and only then plan learning experiences. This supports an outcomes-aligned, evidence-driven curriculum architecture with clearly defined assessment points, which is exactly what accreditation reviewers look for."
SUBHEADING: Student engagement strategies
Paragraph: "Carini RM, Kuh GD & Klein SP (2006), \"Student Engagement and Student Learning: Testing the Linkages\", Research in Higher Education. Empirically links student engagement to critical thinking, grades and persistence. This justifies the curriculum's engagement-oriented strategies, including the three to five discussion topics maintained in every course."

HEADING: 6. Recommendations Before the Accreditation Visit
Numbered list (1-6):
1. "Strengthen staffing in the four non-compliant courses. Foundations of Finance (Fall 2013) needs at least 4 faculty (currently 2) to bring its 1,141.50:1 ratio within the 600:1 limit; Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014) needs at least 5 (currently 3); Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014) needs at least 3 (currently 2); Foundations of Finance (Spring 2014) needs at least 3 (currently 2)."
2. "Appoint a teacher of record for Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014), which is currently staffed only by two teaching assistants."
3. "Introduce quiz-based assessment in the 8 courses that currently have none — all three Environmental Economics & Ethics sections, three of the four Data-Driven Design sections, plus one Applied Analytics and one Biochemistry section — so that all three required assessment types (quiz, assignment, discussion) are present in every course."
4. "Rebalance faculty distribution. The institution-wide average ratio of 488.65:1 sits close to the 600:1 ceiling, and four large-enrolment courses are only marginally compliant: Biochemistry & Bioinformatics Fall 2013 (559.25:1), Fall 2014 (573.00:1) and Spring 2013 (589.00:1), and Foundations of Finance Fall 2014 (591.25:1). These should be monitored and given staffing priority."
5. "Formally record the five scholarly references above in the curriculum dossier to evidence the research-integration requirement at the visit."
6. "Re-run this audit once remediation is complete, so that a 100% course compliance rate can be demonstrated to the review panel."

Closing paragraph: "Full course-by-course data is available in the accompanying workbook, Curriculum_Review.xlsx (sheets: Course Compliance, Literature Support, Summary)."
=== END OF CONTENT ===
